newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas pares losses, still down late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas pares losses, still down late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared some losses but remained lower late Friday in moderate trade, still pressured by some follow-through profit taking in the face of softer weekend cash prices, industry sources said.
At 1430 EDT, June, which dove to $2.195 by midday, was still down by 3.8 cents at $2.235 per mmBtu. July was 4.8 cents lower at $2.24. Others also were lower.

"I think $2.40 (basis June) was overdone and people are taking profits. The weather is just average and that's got to be bearish. We may have seen the highs for a while," said one Texas-based trader, noting lower weekend cash prices.

Temperatures in the East and Midwest are expected to remain below normal this weekend before moderating by early next week. In the Southwest, temperatures are forecast to remain above normal for the next few days.
Most agreed the loss of heating load in the Midwest next week may be enough to tilt the supply-demand balance slightly in favor of the bears.
But few expected prices to crater, with steady injection demand and broader cooling loads likely later in the month.

Technically, traders pegged support in June first at $2.195-2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.04. Resistance was seen at the new high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend cash prices slipped by about a nickel to the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were down by about the same amount to the $2.04-09 range. New York city gate gas lost a few cents to the mid-$2.50s.
NYMEX said 14,765 contracts traded at 1130 EDT.
On the KCBT, June was down by 6.8 cents at $2.075, while deferreds were steady to 6.6 cents lower. The East/West spread widened by three cents to 16.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
